steps.do: Before you start: set CALIBER_FEATURE_RELEASE_CANDIDATES=true on the CALIBER server and restart it; the release signoff factory is off by default. This scenario is an operator process that ends in the in-product Releases record (a Preview, record-only page — signing off records a decision and deploys nothing). Start by opening the staging sheet run-id-manifest.json. You will paste real evidence references (run ids, review states) into it across the next steps, then enter them on the release candidate. Leave a field empty until you have verified it — an empty required field means that evidence is missing.
steps.see: The manifest is open with one block per upstream scenario (SCN-07, SCN-08, SCN-09, SCN-10) and an allure block, all empty and ready to fill.

steps.do: Collect the scorecard run id for each required scenario. Open Evaluations (under Prompt lifecycle) and find each upstream scenario's scorecard run in the table. Copy its run id into the matching eval_run_id field in the manifest. Then open each run and confirm by hand that its pass rate clears that scenario's bar — the pass ≥ … chip on the run detail is a per-row threshold, not a run-level verdict. CALIBER does not compute a single run-level pass/fail gate (the Evaluations table has no gate column), so the go/no-go judgment on each scorecard is yours.
fill: the SCN-07 support-triage scorecard run id
the SCN-08 incident-response scorecard run id
the SCN-09 workflow-debugger scorecard run id
the SCN-10 judge-certification scorecard run id
steps.see: Each scenario row in the manifest now carries a real eval_run_id; you have clicked into each run and judged by hand that its pass rate clears that scenario's bar.

steps.do: Confirm review coverage. Open Review Queues (under Operate) and check that each required queue from the upstream scenarios (e.g. SCN-10's faithfulness-certification) is fully answered with no unresolved items. Set review_queue_complete to true only for queues that are completely answered.
fill: true only where every item in that scenario's required queue is answered
steps.see: Each scenario's review_queue_complete reflects the real queue state; any queue with open items stays false.

steps.do: Re-run the high-risk slices to prove they still pass. From Workflows (under Agent resources) open each workflow and click Run Pipeline (labelled Queue Run when queued execution is enabled) to re-execute the critical subsets — the SCN-07 approval branch (its human_approval gate pauses the run; clear it with Approve then Resume in the run's approval panel), the SCN-08 rollback path, and the SCN-09 retry/resume recovery. Record each fresh run id in the manifest's approval_branch_run_id field for that scenario.
fill: fresh run id from re-running the approval branch
fresh run id from re-running the rollback path
fresh run id from re-running the retry/resume recovery
steps.see: Each critical slice has a fresh, successful run id recorded; you can open each in the workflow's run history and its trace in Observability.

steps.where: Prompt lifecycle › Releases › Release signoff factory › New candidate
steps.do: Create the release candidate. Click Releases under Prompt lifecycle, scroll to the Release signoff factory section (a note says signing off records a decision and deploys nothing) and click New candidate. Enter the candidate name, artifact type, Artifact ID or registry name, Candidate version, Rollback version, and the required score; then edit the criteria JSON (keys, weights, observed scores, thresholds, blocking flags — mirror release-rubric.json) and the evidence JSON (the run ids and review states from your manifest). The planned action is not a field: the UI records promote_<type> → prod. Click Create and evaluate candidate.
fill: artifact type / Artifact ID or registry name / Candidate version
e.g. Workflow / your SCN-07 workflow id / the version you are releasing
the version to fall back to
steps.see: A candidate card appears with a status badge (ready or blocked), the server-computed weighted score as a percentage, and counts of criteria, evidence and blockers plus the rollback version. The server recomputes score and blockers; the browser's numbers are not trusted.

steps.where: Prompt lifecycle › Releases › Release signoff factory › candidate
steps.do: Work any blockers. A blocked candidate has a blocking criterion below its threshold. Do not inflate an observed score — scores are fixed when the candidate is created and there is no edit route, so new evidence means a new candidate. Re-evaluate recomputes from the stored criteria and waivers. If policy permits an exception, an admin enters the criterion key and a reason (at least 8 characters; write any expiry and compensating control into the reason — the UI has no expiry field) and clicks Record waiver.
fill: why the exception is acceptable, who owns it, and when it expires
steps.see: The waived criterion leaves the blocker list and the candidate becomes ready if the score still reaches the required score; the waiver is audited with the approving admin.

steps.where: Prompt lifecycle › Releases › Release signoff factory › candidate
steps.do: Generate the release evidence. Click Generate Allure on the candidate card. CALIBER creates a durable Allure-compatible JSON report job with a SHA-256 of the candidate snapshot and shows "Allure report … generated and retained." Record the report job id. (The static Allure HTML under Admin › Settings › Allure Report is separate CI evidence produced by make allure-report; it is not needed to sign this candidate.)
steps.see: The card reports the new report job id; the report snapshot hash covers the candidate as it is now (generate it after any waiver).

steps.where: Prompt lifecycle › Releases › Release signoff factory › candidate
steps.do: Record the decision. As an admin, type an accountable Signoff rationale (at least 8 characters; decision-record.template.md is an optional drafting aid) and click Sign off GO — enabled only while the candidate is ready — or Sign off NO-GO. The final snapshot is immutable; create a new candidate for a changed release package. Nothing is deployed or rolled back: the page is record-only.
fill: cite the evidence by id/name; for NO-GO name the failing criterion and the owning scenario
steps.see: The candidate moves to signed_go (or signed_no_go) and its Sign off controls disappear.

steps.do: (Optional) If issues surfaced and you need to triage which are true blockers, create a triage queue. Click + New Queue and add the questions from blocker-questions.json (use the + Add question button for each; map the type values bool → pass_fail and str → text/categorical). Enqueue the candidate trace ids in the Add traces to review field and answer them — answers write back onto each trace.
fill: Triage candidate release blockers: confirm whether each is a true release blocker, who owns it, and (if waived) when the waiver expires.
is_release_blocker (pass_fail), owning_scenario (text), severity (text), waiver_granted (pass_fail), waiver_expiry (text), waiver_owner (text) — paste from blocker-questions.json
steps.see: A release-blocker-triage queue exists; answered items record, per blocker, whether it blocks the release, its owner, and any waiver.

steps.do: (Optional) To draft the signoff rationale from your evidence, register the summarizer prompt. Open Prompts (under Prompt lifecycle), click New prompt, and paste the template body (everything below the YAML frontmatter) from release-risk-summarizer.md. It only narrates evidence you supply and is hard-wired to force no_go on missing evidence or open blockers — it never invents passing evidence.
fill: v1 release-risk summarizer (evidence-in, decision-out, no invention)
steps.see: A release-risk-summarizer prompt is registered; feed it your filled manifest to draft the rationale (it returns JSON only).
